name: chat_typical
use_case: Conversational turn carrying a short history and a system prompt.
rationale: Representative of a general assistant. Output budget matches the published reasoning protocol, so the only difference from the legacy headline shape is the input.
duplicate_note: These indices repeat an earlier prompt verbatim, on purpose. With prefix caching OFF they are indistinguishable from any other prompt. With it ON they are the only prompts able to hit the cache, which is how to measure the caching effect without contaminating the uncached figure.
prompts:
(context ref c27485-000)

[c27485:000.00] Admission control belongs at the edge of a system, before a request has consumed any expensive resource. Rejecting a request after it has already acquired a database connection and a worker thread converts an overload into a resource leak, because the cost was paid and the work discarded.

[c27485:000.01] Backpressure has to propagate to the point where work is admitted, not merely to the point where it is queued. A component that accepts requests into an unbounded buffer converts an overload into unbounded latency, which is harder to diagnose than an outright rejection and defeats every downstream timeout budget.

[c27485:000.02] Speculative execution hides tail latency by issuing duplicate work and taking the first answer. It is only sound when the work is idempotent and when the cluster has spare capacity: under saturation the duplicates compete with the originals and make the tail worse rather than better.

[c27485:000.03] Vector clocks detect concurrent updates without a global ordering, but they grow with the number of writers and cannot by themselves decide which concurrent value should win. Systems that expose them push that decision to the application; systems that hide them usually resolve by last-writer-wins on a physical timestamp and accept the silent loss of one update.

[c27485:000.04] Branch predictors trade table area for accuracy. A two-level adaptive predictor keys a pattern-history table on recent global branch outcomes, capturing correlations that a per-branch counter cannot see. Mispredictions cost the full pipeline depth, so on a deep out-of-order core a one percent accuracy improvement can outweigh a substantial increase in predictor storage.

[c27485:000.05] A service mesh sidecar terminates connections on behalf of the workload, which moves retry, timeout and circuit-breaking policy out of application code. The cost is a second network hop and a second failure domain: a sidecar that has not finished loading its configuration will reject traffic that the workload is perfectly able to serve, so readiness must gate on the sidecar rather than the application.

Summarise the material above, then answer: which approach would you choose for a system with strict tail-latency requirements, and what would you give up?

[338d93:001.01] Copy-on-write snapshots let a filesystem present a stable view while writes continue.
